releases.theme: Config correctness and project identity: make the generated config.toml load and work, point the project at the real upstream, and add changelog/ignore scaffolding.
releases.rationale: Backward-compatible bug-fix + additive hygiene, so a MINOR bump. The repo exists to emit one correct ~/.codex/config.toml, and today it is wrong in ways verified against the installed Codex CLI 0.135.0: base_url embeds the full /v1/chat/completions path (docs already use the clean /v1 root at docs/reference/models.md:154, so the script disagrees with its own docs) and no wire_api is set. CRITICAL CORRECTION to three of the five council proposals: I empirically tested `codex --strict-config doctor` against a sandboxed config and `wire_api = "chat"` is REJECTED (config fails to load) while `wire_api = "responses"` LOADS. The guide's prose (CODEX_CLI_SETUP_GUIDE.md:140-143) saying responses is the standard and chat is deprecated is therefore CORRECT, and any item proposing wire_api='chat' would actively break config loading. We standardize on wire_api='responses'. We also remove the script's wrong-credential instruction ('Add your OPENAI_API_KEY to ~/.codex/auth.json', line 185 — this setup uses NEBIUS_API_KEY only), fix the dead nebius-skill guide URL the script prints (line 195), relabel the 'Nebius Fast (Mistral)' provider that actually points at Gemma (lines 87/105), correct the README's shashikant86 link to openai/codex, and add CHANGELOG.md + .gitignore. disable_tools is deliberately NOT reintroduced: it exists nowhere in the tracked tree (only in plans/ORCHESTRATION.md notes) and was removed after commit d7ad935; restoring an undocumented key from rolled-back history is out of scope. File ownership is strictly disjoint: the script item solely owns setup-codex-nebius.sh; the identity item solely owns README.md; the hygiene item owns only new files.

releases.theme: Make it verifiable and keep the docs site buildable: a HOME-sandboxed test suite, GitHub Actions CI, and a Mintlify navigation that matches reality.
releases.rationale: Still backward-compatible/additive, so a MINOR bump. The v1.1 correctness fixes are only durable if enforced; the 'fix'/'oops' commits in git history prove broken edits reach main unchecked. This release adds a pure-bash test harness that always runs setup-codex-nebius.sh under HOME=$(mktemp -d) with a stubbed `codex` on PATH (the script's Step 1 hard-exits if `codex` is absent — verified — so CI must stub it), plus a GitHub Actions workflow (ShellCheck + tests + a nav-vs-files guard), and fixes the Mintlify site: mint.json lists 17 navigation slugs but only 6 backing docs exist (verified), and 5 of those 6 docs contain dangling intra-doc links to pages that do not exist. CORRECTION to two proposals: the docs are .md and Mintlify resolves BARE nav slugs (no extension) to .md or .mdx — there is NO requirement to rename .md to .mdx, and doing so risks breaking working pages; the fix is to PRUNE nav to the 6 real pages and repair the dangling links, not to rename. File ownership is strictly disjoint: the test item owns only new files under tests/; the CI item owns only files under .github/; the docs item owns mint.json plus exactly the 5 docs files that contain dangling links (docs/reference/models.md is intentionally excluded so it stays free for v2.0's model refresh).

items.title: HOME-sandboxed pure-bash test suite with a codex stub
items.description: Create a test harness under tests/ exercising setup-codex-nebius.sh entirely inside a throwaway HOME. HARD REQUIREMENT: every invocation MUST set HOME=$(mktemp -d) (cleaned up via trap) so the real ~/.codex and shell profiles are never read or written. The script must be driven non-interactively with `printf 'testkey\nn\n' | HOME=$tmp bash setup-codex-nebius.sh` (feed a fake key, then 'n' to decline the connection test so no network call happens) — do NOT pipe </dev/null (verified to hit EOF and abort under set -e before config is created). Because the script's Step 1 (line 14) hard-exits if `codex` is not on PATH, the harness MUST prepend a temp bin dir containing an executable `codex` stub (a 2-line shell script printing a fake version like 'codex-cli 0.0.0-test') to PATH so tests are deterministic without the real CLI. Provide tests/run.sh (plain bash assertions, no external deps) as the entrypoint covering at minimum: (a) the script creates $HOME/.codex/config.toml and exits 0; (b) base_url has no '/chat/completions' and wire_api='responses' appears twice; (c) no OPENAI_API_KEY/auth.json text in the script; (d) idempotency: running twice into the same sandbox HOME leaves exactly one `export NEBIUS_API_KEY=` line in the written profile; (e) the entered key value is never echoed to stdout (capture output, grep for the fake key, expect none). Add an optional config-validity check: if a `codex` binary is genuinely present AND not the stub (detect via a CODEX_REAL env or `command -v codex` plus a version check), run `CODEX_HOME=$HOME/.codex codex --strict-config doctor` and assert it reports config loaded; otherwise skip gracefully. Add tests/README.md documenting the mandatory HOME-sandbox rule and the printf-driver pattern. Do NOT modify setup-codex-nebius.sh, mint.json, .github/, or docs.

items.title: GitHub Actions CI: ShellCheck + sandboxed tests + nav guard
items.description: Create ONLY .github/workflows/ci.yml, triggered on push and pull_request, ubuntu-latest, requiring no secrets and no network to Token Factory. Jobs: (1) lint — install ShellCheck (preinstalled on ubuntu-latest or via apt) and run `shellcheck setup-codex-nebius.sh tests/*.sh`; configure to fail on errors (warnings may be allowed by passing a severity or inline disables — pin the chosen severity in the workflow). (2) test — run `bash tests/run.sh` (the harness sandboxes HOME and stubs codex itself; as belt-and-suspenders also export `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` at the job level). The real codex CLI is NOT installed in CI, so the harness's stub is what makes Step 1 pass — do not add a codex install step. (3) nav-guard — an inline bash/python step that parses the navigation page slugs from mint.json and asserts every slug maps to an existing docs/<slug>.md file, failing if any nav entry lacks a backing file or any docs page is missing from nav. Pin actions to a major version (actions/checkout@v4). Keep it pure YAML. Do NOT create or modify mint.json, tests/, docs, or the script; rely on the other items having produced tests/run.sh and a corrected mint.json (this release's docs item).

items.title: Prune mint.json navigation to real pages and repair dangling intra-doc links
items.description: Make the Mintlify site coherent WITHOUT renaming any files (Mintlify resolves bare nav slugs to .md — verified; do NOT convert .md to .mdx). (1) In mint.json, prune navigation[].pages so every remaining slug maps to a file that exists: keep introduction, quick-start, installation, usage/basic-commands, reference/models, troubleshooting/common-issues; REMOVE the 11 slugs with no backing file: setup/overview, setup/manual-configuration, setup/environment-variables, setup/testing-connection, usage/profiles, usage/editor-integration, usage/git-integration, reference/configuration, reference/api-endpoints, troubleshooting/authentication, troubleshooting/connection-errors. (2) For the logo/favicon (mint.json references /logo/dark.svg, /logo/light.svg, /favicon.png which do not exist): the simplest honest fix is to REMOVE the 'logo' and 'favicon' keys from mint.json so the build does not reference missing assets (Mintlify falls back to defaults). (3) Repair every dangling intra-doc link in the 5 docs files that point at now-removed pages, by repointing to an existing page or removing the link: docs/introduction.md:45 (./setup/overview); docs/installation.md:159 (./usage/editor-integration); docs/quick-start.md:98-100,108 (editor-integration, git-integration, profiles, authentication); docs/usage/basic-commands.md:185-187,193 (profiles, editor-integration, git-integration, api-endpoints); docs/troubleshooting/common-issues.md:78,195,196 (authentication, connection-errors). After this item, no docs page links to a removed slug. Do NOT edit docs/reference/models.md (reserved for v2.0 model refresh — it has zero dangling links, verified), README.md, CODEX_CLI_SETUP_GUIDE.md, the CI workflow, or the test files.

The harness asserts the v1.1 invariants (no '/chat/completions' in base_url, wire_api='responses' present) AND idempotency (a second run does not duplicate the NEBIUS_API_KEY export line).

releases.theme: The coherent 2.0: a breaking provider-config cleanup, a verified-fresh model catalog, and a fully reconciled docs set that agrees with the shipped config.
releases.rationale: MAJOR bump and the required final version, exactly v2.0. A major is justified by a BREAKING change to the generated configuration: the redundant nebius_fast provider (which only differs from nebius_token_factory by the now-removed 'Mistral' label) is consolidated so all three profiles reference a single nebius_token_factory provider, and provider/profile identifiers are normalized — changing keys that an existing ~/.codex/config.toml and any user `--profile` invocations depend on, so semver mandates a major and a migration note. Bundled with that: refresh the possibly-stale model catalog (Hermes-4-405B / Gemma-3-27b-it / Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct) and reconcile the long-form guide, which is the LAST place that still contradicts the shipped config — it has the api.nebius.ai host (lines 307 and 431, both must change to api.tokenfactory.nebius.com), an Ollama local-server fallback and an NPM-wrapper aside that nudge toward unsupported/forbidden patterns, Node v16+ (line 20) vs the docs' Node 22+, and stale base_url examples. NOTE: the guide's wire_api section (140-143) is actually CORRECT (responses) per the verified strict-config test, so it should be KEPT/aligned, not reversed. The narrative: '1.x = correct, tested, and buildable; 2.0 = consolidated, current, and internally consistent.' File ownership is strictly disjoint: the config-redesign item solely owns setup-codex-nebius.sh; the model-catalog item solely owns docs/reference/models.md; the guide item solely owns CODEX_CLI_SETUP_GUIDE.md; the release-cut item owns CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE, and README.md.

rationale:
This is a small bash-script-plus-docs repo whose sole purpose is to emit one correct ~/.codex/config.toml and document it. The honest path to v2.0 is therefore: fix the artifact, prove it stays fixed, then make the docs tell the truth — not add features. I rejected every speculative tangent (TypeScript wrapper, caching flags, editor-integration expansion) and, per the hard constraint and the 2026-06-11 rollback, nothing resembling a proxy/relay/local server appears anywhere — v2.0 even removes the guide's existing Ollama-fallback and NPM-wrapper asides that nudged toward those forbidden patterns.

The single most consequential council disagreement was the wire_api/base_url contract, and three proposals (release-manager, dx-pm) asserted 'wire_api=chat is correct; the guide is factually backwards.' I verified this empirically against the installed Codex CLI 0.135.0 using `codex --strict-config doctor` on sandboxed configs: wire_api='chat' is REJECTED (config fails to load), wire_api='responses' LOADS, and 'bogus' is rejected too (the value is enum-validated). So the guide (lines 140-143) is CORRECT and I standardized on wire_api='responses' across script and docs, with `codex --strict-config doctor` as an objective, hermetic acceptance gate. I also confirmed disable_tools exists nowhere in the tracked tree (only in plans/), so I dropped the reliability-pm/scope-cutter 'reintroduce disable_tools' items as built on a false premise; and I confirmed Mintlify resolves bare nav slugs to .md, so I dropped the release-manager/scope-cutter '.md->.mdx rename' as unnecessary and risky, adopting the dx-pm/docs-pm 'prune nav + fix dangling links' approach instead.

Sequencing follows strict semver and dependency order: v1.1 (MINOR) ships the backward-compatible config-correctness + identity fixes the artifact needs (base_url root, wire_api=responses, drop the wrong OPENAI_API_KEY/auth.json instruction, fix the dead nebius-skill URL and the Mistral/Gemma mislabel, correct the README upstream link) plus CHANGELOG/.gitignore. v1.2 (MINOR) makes it durable: a test suite that always runs under HOME=$(mktemp -d) with a stubbed codex (the script hard-exits without codex on PATH — verified), ShellCheck+nav CI, and a buildable Mintlify site (nav pruned to the 6 real pages, dangling links repaired). v2.0 (MAJOR, exactly the required final version) is a genuine breaking change — consolidating to a single provider normalizes keys that existing configs/--profile calls depend on — bundled with the model refresh and the final guide reconciliation (the last place api.nebius.ai, the Ollama fallback, and the shashikant disclaimer live).

Constraint enforcement I performed myself: final release is exactly v2.0; 4 releases (baseline + 3); each release has <=4 items; within every release the item file sets are strictly DISJOINT (I rejected the faked disjointness in three proposals that split setup-codex-nebius.sh across multiple parallel items or assigned phantom sidecar files — the script is owned by exactly one item per release, and in v1.2/v2.0 docs/reference/models.md is deliberately reserved to a single owner to avoid the Mintlify-vs-model-refresh collision). No item touches plans/. All file paths referenced exist in the repo or are explicitly new. Every test plan uses the verified printf 'testkey\nn\n' driver (NOT </dev/null, which I confirmed aborts under set -e before config.toml is created) and overrides HOME so the real ~/.codex and shell profiles are never modified.
handoffNotes:
ORDERING AND CROSS-RELEASE HAZARDS for implementing agents:

1) BASELINE COMMIT: All five input proposals wrongly claimed HEAD == 4f2f98f. Verified actual HEAD is 84f90e4, which adds ONLY plans/. Tag v1.0 at 8801e31 (recommended: last clean script+docs commit) so the tag does NOT include plans/. Do not `git push` history; only the annotated tag. The operator (not an item) creates all tags.

2) setup-codex-nebius.sh is edited in BOTH v1.1 (fix-generated-config) and v2.0 (consolidate-provider-config). This is safe ONLY because releases are sequential. The v2.0 edit assumes v1.1 already landed (base_url=/v1, wire_api=responses, no auth.json line, provider relabeled). Do not run them in parallel.

3) wire_api MUST be 'responses', never 'chat'. This was verified live: `codex --strict-config doctor` rejects wire_api='chat' (config fails to load) and accepts 'responses'. The acceptance gate `codex --strict-config doctor` is the objective check. If a future agent 'helpfully' changes it to 'chat', CI/acceptance will (and should) fail.

4) disable_tools: DO NOT add it. It is not in the tracked tree (only in plans/ORCHESTRATION.md as historical context) and was removed after commit d7ad935. Several council proposals wanted to 'reintroduce' it — ignore that; it is unsourced and the responses wire_api is the actual serialization fix path.

5) TEST INVOCATION: Never drive the script with `</dev/null`. Verified: the `read -sp` on line 37 hits EOF, `set -e` aborts at Step 3, and config.toml is NEVER created — every downstream assertion then fails. Use `printf 'testkey\nn\n' | HOME=$(mktemp -d) bash setup-codex-nebius.sh`. Also: the script's Step 1 (line 14) hard-exits if `codex` is not on PATH, so the test harness MUST prepend a `codex` stub to PATH; CI (ubuntu-latest, no codex installed) depends on this stub — do not add a real codex install step to CI.

6) Do NOT upgrade `set -e` to `set -euo pipefail` in v1.1 or v1.2. The interactive `read` calls abort under -u/EOF and would break the verified happy path; no item requests this change. If a future hardening release wants it, it must also add EOF guards to the reads, but that is out of scope here.

7) DISJOINT-FILE enforcement within a release is real (items run as parallel agents in one worktree). Note specifically: in v1.2, fix-mintlify-nav owns docs/introduction.md, quick-start.md, installation.md, usage/basic-commands.md, troubleshooting/common-issues.md and mint.json — but NOT docs/reference/models.md, which is intentionally reserved so v2.0's refresh-model-catalog can own it cleanly. In v2.0, the three model_name strings must match byte-for-byte across four files written by three different items (consolidate-provider-config -> script; refresh-model-catalog -> models.md; cut-v2-release -> README.md; reconcile-setup-guide -> guide). Treat docs/reference/models.md as the source of truth for those exact strings; if any model cannot be verified against the live Token Factory catalog, KEEP the existing IDs in all four rather than inventing new ones (no item can hit the live catalog in CI).

8) The .gitignore item must NOT add plans/ (it is tracked + orchestrator-reserved) and must NOT delete the existing .pytest_cache/ directory (only ignore it). README host normalization: mint.json uses nebius.com; README/guide have stray nebius.ai links — normalize to nebius.com where they are project/marketing links (the api host is api.tokenfactory.nebius.com, distinct).
